transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi… yeah, thanks for seeing me. I guess what brought me in is that I’m having a really hard time finishing things properly at work, even when I know they’re important. Like I’ll start the sanitation steps, or I’ll be doing batch logs, or the end-of-line paperwork, and I know the whole process matters, but somehow I leave out the last parts. Not because I don’t care—I really do care—but I’ll think I’m done, or I’ll move on to the next thing, and then later it turns out I didn’t complete something.

And it’s embarrassing because these aren’t optional things. My job depends on them being finished correctly, and I know that. I’ll start out trying to be careful, but then by the end, it’s like the final pieces just don’t get done unless someone catches it or I go back and realize it. It’s been stressing me out a lot, because I don’t want to be seen as careless or unreliable.
When you miss the last steps, is it because you get caught up checking or rechecking things over and over?

I don’t think so… at least, not in the way you’re describing. Like, I’m not usually stuck there checking the same thing over and over and unable to move on. It’s more like I’ll think I’ve done it, or I’ll get pulled into whatever the next part is, and then later realize I didn’t actually finish the last bit.

I do sometimes look back at things if I’m worried, but I wouldn’t say the problem is me rechecking too much. It’s more that the ending of the task somehow slips away from me, if that makes sense. Like the “final step” doesn’t feel as obvious in the moment as it does afterward when someone points it out.
Did you have similar trouble finishing tasks or missing details when you were a child?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, looking back, it wasn’t like this is brand new. My mom actually still has some of my old elementary school report cards, and there are comments from around fourth grade where the teachers basically said I was bright, but I needed constant reminders to finish my classwork and actually turn in my homework.

I remember that pretty clearly too, because I usually understood what was being taught. It wasn’t like I didn’t get the lesson. I’d be sitting there and I could answer questions or follow along, but then when it came to doing the actual assignment, I’d miss parts of the instructions or skip over a section without realizing it. If the teacher was nearby or kind of keeping me on track, I did better, but if I was left to just do it on my own, I’d lose pieces of what I was supposed to do.

And with homework, I remember finishing some of it and then somehow not turning it in, or thinking it was done but there was some part missing. So yes, there were definitely signs of that when I was a kid.
As a child, were you often fidgety or unable to stay seated when you were expected to?

I’m not really sure about that one. I don’t remember being the kind of kid who was constantly out of my seat or running around when I wasn’t supposed to. At least, nobody in my family talks about me that way, and I don’t remember teachers making a big issue out of me not staying seated.

I mean, I probably moved around like any kid—shifting in my chair, playing with pencils, that kind of thing—but I don’t know that it was “often” or enough that people noticed it as a problem. The things I remember being pointed out were more about not finishing work or needing reminders, not so much me physically not sitting still.
Do you find yourself worrying excessively about a lot of different things, even when there isn’t a clear reason to?

I’m not sure I’d describe it that way, no. I mean, I do worry about things sometimes, like anyone does, especially if there’s an actual reason or something coming up that I need to deal with. But I don’t feel like I’m constantly worrying about lots of different areas of my life for no clear reason.

Like, if something is unfinished or if I know I’ve forgotten something, then yeah, I might stress about that. But it doesn’t feel like this broad, nonstop worrying where my mind is jumping from one fear to another all day. I guess I’d say my stress usually has a trigger, or at least it feels connected to something specific, not just worry out of nowhere.
Have you had periods lasting at least two weeks when you felt depressed or down most of the day nearly every day?

I don’t think so… not in that kind of clear, two-weeks-straight way. I mean, I’ve definitely had days where I feel low or frustrated or just kind of worn out, especially when things are piling up and I feel like I’m not keeping up, but I don’t remember a period where I was depressed most of the day nearly every day for at least two weeks.

I’m trying to think carefully, because sometimes it’s hard to separate being stressed or discouraged from being actually depressed, if that makes sense. But no, I don’t think I’ve had that sustained kind of down mood you’re describing.
